title: Mobility improved after stroke when a robotic device was used in comparison to physical therapy - The MOST Study
summary:
Stroke is the most common cause of chronic disability. It can affect aspects of daily life, e.g., grasping, language, walking. Lower extremity paresis after stroke reduces the quality of life since independent mobility within the community is restricted. Improved walking is the most frequently stated goal of patients suffering from a stroke. In the past, different types of rehabilitation and sophisticated interventions have been developed to improve lower extremity function in stroke patients, e.g., treadmill training with partial body weight support, a lower extremity robot termed Lokomat, electromechanical gait trainer plus physiotherapy, combined peripheral nerve and brain stimulation and treadmill training with partial body weight support in patients with spinal cord injury.
Recently Ekso Bionics® (EB) developed a robot for lower extremity training of stroke patients. Stroke patients provided with EB are able to walk with high step dosages. Gait training is possible even when patients are not able to walk alone. EB engages patients by challenging their abilities; balancing the physical effort they exert with the amount of help they need to achieve a more normalized gait.
But still now a randomized control study is lacking to investigate whether EB is more beneficial in comparison to a conventional physiotherapy. In a conventional physiotherapy physiotherapists (one or two) help patients to walk, or use specific patient handling skills to guide patients through initiation and completion of intended tasks to promote motor learning for efficient motor control in various environments (e.g. by the use of the Bobath concept or neuro-developmental treatment). Furthermore, a recent Cochrane analysis showed that stroke patients who are not able to walk independently, they do not benefit from treadmill with and without body weight support. Therefore, the effect of EB on walking in stroke patients without ability to walk is of interest.
conditions: Cerebral infarction due to thrombosis of cerebral arteries

interventions.name: Inervention group (IG) with Eksoskeltt (Ekso Bionics): 45 minutes daily training from monday to friday for three weeks

Control group (CG: conventional physiotherapy): 45 minutes daily training from monday to friday for three weeks in conventional physiotherapy programm which includes fasclitation, trunc controll training, at least 20min walking with personal and/or devices aid (with the exception of Ekso)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- First ever stroke within last 3 months
- Stroke patients who are not able to walk alone
Exclusion criteria:
- Body weight above 120kg 
- Orthopedic problems and spasticity which make it impossible to walk with EB   
- cardio-pulmonary not tenable
- patients with aphasia, who don’t understand instructions
- patients with neglect
